title: Operators, precedence, and short-circuit evaluation
hook: Operators turn values into expressions. JavaScript adds loose equality (==), strict equality (===), nullish coalescing (??), and optional chaining (?.) — plus precedence traps where ?? and || or ?: mix without parentheses bite production code.

blocks.text: An **expression** is code that evaluates to a value: `5 + 3` yields `8`. An **operator** is the symbol that performs the action: `+`, `===`, `&&`, `??`. JavaScript operators follow a **precedence** table — multiplication before addition, for example. Unlike C#, JavaScript **coerces types** for `==`, `+` with strings, and logical operators treat values as **truthy** or **falsy** rather than requiring bool.

entries.plainDefinition: Returns the right value only when the left is null or undefined — not for other falsy values like 0 or "".
Short-circuits to undefined when the receiver is null or undefined before accessing a property or calling a method.
entries.example: user?.profile?.email — undefined if user or profile is nullish.

entries.plainDefinition: && and || stop evaluating once the result is decided. ?? stops when the left is not nullish.
entries.example: user && user.isActive — isActive is not read when user is falsy.

entries.plainDefinition: Rules that decide which operator binds tighter when parentheses are omitted.
entries.example: a ?? b || c is parsed as (a ?? b) || c — often not what authors intend.

sections.heading: Why operator choice matters in production

blocks.text: Use **===** and **!==** for equality checks — avoid == except when you explicitly want coercion rules. Use **??** for null/undefined defaults; use **||** only when every falsy value should fall through (0, "", false). **Optional chaining** (?.) prevents TypeError on nested API payloads. **Precedence traps**: ?? has lower precedence than && and || but mixes oddly with ?: — always parenthesize mixed expressions. The exponent operator `**` binds tighter than unary minus: `-2 ** 2` is `-4`, not `4`.

blocks.title: C# comparison
blocks.body: C# == is always strict and typed like JavaScript ===. C# has ?? and ?. but no == coercion. JavaScript == converts operands until types match or comparison fails — a top interview trap for C# developers.

items.title: Parentheses first
items.body: Anything inside ( ) runs before anything outside — your safest tool.

items.title: Unary, multiplicative, additive
items.body: !, typeof, ++, then *, /, %, then +, -. Note: + concatenates if either operand is a string.

items.title: Logical and nullish
items.body: &&, then ||, then ??. Mixing ?? with || or ?: without parens is a common bug.

diagram.title: Optional chaining short-circuit
diagram.source:
flowchart TD
  A[Evaluate receiver] --> B{Is null or undefined?}
  B -->|Yes| C[Return undefined — skip rest]
  B -->|No| D[Access property or call method]
  D --> E[Return result]

sections.heading: Code walkthrough: arithmetic, equality, and nullish operators

snippet.label: Strict vs loose equality
snippet.code:
5 == "5";   // true — coercion
5 === "5";  // false — strict

null == undefined;  // true
null === undefined; // false

[] == false;  // true — obscure coercion
[] === false; // false — always prefer this form
snippet.explanation: === compares without coercion. == applies Abstract Equality Comparison rules — memorize the safe rule: use === unless you know exactly why == is required.

snippet.label: ?? vs || and optional chaining
snippet.explanation: ?? is for nullish defaults. || treats 0 and "" as missing. ?. stops at null/undefined receivers — similar to C# ?. but returns undefined, not null.

snippet.label: Precedence trap — ?? with || and ?:
snippet.explanation: ?? cannot mix with && or || without parentheses — SyntaxError in modern engines if ambiguous. When in doubt, add explicit parens like C# style for ?: and ??.

snippet.label: Short-circuit guards and typeof edge
snippet.explanation: && chains guards like C# && but accepts truthy/falsy, not bool only. + prefers string concat if either side is string; other arithmetic operators coerce to number.

blocks.title: Precedence traps that fail interviews
blocks.body: Writing a ?? b || c expecting b to win for all falsy a — parsing is (a ?? b) || c. Using || for numeric defaults when 0 is valid. Using == because 'it works' — [] == false and null == undefined surprise teams. Assuming ?. evaluates the entire chain when middle is null — it short-circuits to undefined. Mixing ?? with && without parentheses — syntax error.

blocks.title: C# developer cheat sheet
blocks.body: Replace C# == with JavaScript ===. Replace C# ?? with JavaScript ?? but remember JS also has undefined. Replace C# ?. with JavaScript ?. — similar ergonomics, undefined instead of null. There is no C# 14 x?.Prop = v in JavaScript.

interviewTakeaways: === is strict; == coerces — treat == as deprecated in new code.
?? defaults only null/undefined; || defaults all falsy values including 0 and "".
?. short-circuits to undefined; does not call methods on nullish receivers.
60s: C# == equals JS ===. ?? vs || is the production trap. Parenthesize ?? with || or ?:. Optional chaining has no left-hand assignment.
Follow-up: what is the difference between null == undefined and null === undefined?
commonPitfalls: Weak: 'I use == for convenience' — fails on [] == false and string-number surprises.
Weak: '?? and || are interchangeable' — 0 and "" behave differently.
Strong: '=== always unless spec requires ==. ?? for nullish API fields. Parenthesize mixed nullish/logical/ternary expressions.'

jsTsCorrelations.note: C# == is strict like JS ===. C# ?? matches JS ?? for null but C# has no undefined. C# 14 ?. assignment has no JS equivalent.
TypeScript optional chaining narrows types after ?. checks. eslint eqeqeq recommends ===. Nullish coalescing types exclude null and undefined from the left side.
